title: Grade 6 Science — Tue, Jun 17
description: Changes Around Us — Day 2 of 5: Reversible changes
subject: science

questions.question: A reversible change is one that can be ___.
options: Undone to get back the original substance
questions.explanation: A reversible change can be reversed to get back the original substance.

questions.question: Melting of ice is reversible because ___.
options: The water can be frozen back into ice
questions.explanation: Melting is reversible — by cooling water below 0°C, it freezes back into ice (the original substance).

questions.question: Which of these is a reversible change?
questions.explanation: Stretching a rubber band is reversible — when released, it returns to its original shape.

questions.question: Dissolving sugar in water is reversible because ___.
options: The water can be evaporated to recover the sugar
questions.explanation: The sugar can be recovered by heating the solution and evaporating the water — the original substance is obtained.

questions.question: Evaporation of water is a reversible change because ___.
options: Water vapour can condense back into liquid water
questions.explanation: Water evaporates into vapour, and when cooled the vapour condenses back into liquid water — reversible.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reversible change?
questions.explanation: Burning paper is irreversible — it produces ash and gases. The paper cannot be restored.

questions.question: Inflating a balloon is an example of a ___ change.
questions.explanation: Inflating a balloon is reversible — you can deflate it and the balloon returns to its original state.

questions.question: Boiling water to produce steam is a ___ change.
questions.explanation: Boiling is reversible — steam (water vapour) can be cooled to condense back into liquid water.

questions.question: Flattening a ball of clay is ___.
questions.explanation: Flattening clay is a physical change — you can reshape the clay back into a ball. It is reversible.

questions.question: Which change can be reversed by cooling?
questions.explanation: Melted ice cream can be refrozen (cooled) to recover a solid again — reversible change of state.

questions.question: Iron filings attracted to a magnet — is separating them reversible?
options: Yes — the filings can be removed from the magnet
questions.explanation: Magnetic attraction is reversible — the iron filings can be removed. No permanent change occurred.

questions.question: What makes the dissolution of salt in water reversible?
options: No new substance is formed and salt can be recovered by evaporation
questions.explanation: Salt dissolves physically without forming a new substance. Evaporating the water recovers the original salt.

questions.question: Freezing of water is a ___ change.
questions.explanation: Freezing is a change of state (liquid → solid) that is reversible — melt the ice and you get liquid water again.

questions.question: A reversible change is generally a ___ change.
questions.explanation: Reversible changes are generally physical — they change form or state without forming new substances.

questions.question: Which of these is a reversible physical change?
questions.explanation: Dissolving sugar in water is reversible — evaporate the water and you recover the sugar. Baking, burning, and growing are irreversible.
